parts.title: What this worksheet teaches
parts.text: Children read short, decodable sentences that practise the sound for wh. Every other word uses letter-sounds they already know, so they can read each sentence on their own. Reading the page three times builds fluency.

parts.title: How to lead it (about 15 minutes)
text: 1. Say the sound for wh together.
2. Read the first sentence together, pointing under each word.
3. Children underline wh in each sentence, then read each sentence on their own.
4. Children read the whole page three times and colour one face each time.

parts.title: Answer key
text: Your turn / extension: any real word with wh.

parts.title: Ontario curriculum link (official wording)
text: In plain terms: children match a letter to the sound it makes.
A2.5 — read and spell simple words using phonemic awareness and phonics knowledge.
In plain terms: children read and spell simple words by blending the sounds.

parts.title: If children get stuck — and ways to adjust
text: Watch for: sounding out wh part by part. Cover the rest of the word and say the target first.
Make it easier: do fewer items together first; you read, the child echoes.
Make it harder: ask the child to think of or write one more word with the target.
You'll know it worked when: the child reads the page smoothly and spots the target on sight.
